rubric.why: Rewards the definitions of Genetics and Anatomy, including their distinguishing ideas.
rubric.description: Genetics concerns the transfer of characteristics from parents to offspring; Anatomy concerns internal physical structure.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark when both branch names and the key idea of each definition are present.

rubric.why: Rewards the definitions of Palaeontology, Marine Biology and Pathology.
rubric.description: Palaeontology studies fossils; Marine Biology studies life in oceans; Pathology studies diseases, their causes and effects.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark when all three branch names and their defining subjects are present.

modelAnswer: Genetics is the branch of Biology that deals with the study of transfer of characteristics from parents to offspring. Anatomy is the branch of Biology that explores the internal physical structure of organisms, particularly humans. Palaeontology is the branch of Biology that deals with the study of fossils. Marine Biology is the branch of Biology that deals with the study of life in oceans. Pathology is the study of diseases, their causes, and effects.

rubric.why: Identifies the branch of Biology named in the answer.
Checks that the response states what Embryology studies.
rubric.description: It studies the development of an organism from a fertilized egg.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the development-from-a-fertilized-egg idea.

modelAnswer: Embryology is the study of the process of development of organism from fertilized egg.

rubric.why: Checks the defining subject of Morphology.
rubric.description: Morphology is the study of the form and structure of organisms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming Morphology and stating form and structure.

rubric.why: Checks the defining subject of Physiology.
rubric.description: Physiology deals with the functioning of body parts.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming Physiology and stating that it concerns the functioning of body parts.

modelAnswer: Morphology is the study of the form and structure of organisms. Physiology is the branch of Biology that deals with the functioning of body parts.

rubric.why: Rewards the role of making observations and gathering relevant information.
rubric.description: Scientists observe the problem using their senses and study previous research on related problems.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for observations together with a method or source of information, such as the senses or previous research.

rubric.why: Rewards the role of experiments in checking proposed explanations.
rubric.description: Scientists perform experiments to test hypotheses.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark when experiments and testing hypotheses are both stated.

modelAnswer: Scientists make observations about the problem. They use five senses for making observation. They also read and study the previous researches on the same or related problems. Scientists perform experiments to test all hypotheses.

rubric.why: Checks the defining feature of a hypothesis.
rubric.description: A hypothesis is a tentative answer.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as tentative.

rubric.why: Checks what the tentative answer is proposed to address.
rubric.description: It is a tentative answer to a scientific problem.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking the answer to a scientific problem.

modelAnswer: Such tentative answer of scientific problem is called hypothesis.

rubric.why: Checks the defining nature of deductions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that deductions are logical results.

rubric.why: Checks what the deductions are derived from.
rubric.description: Deductions are logical results of hypotheses.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking the results to hypotheses.

modelAnswer: Such logical results of hypotheses are called deductions.
